correctness.rationale: The cap/cylinder volume and polar radial formula reduce exactly to a one-dimensional spherical-coordinate expectation. Integration of a derivative provides A-(d-1)sB=dC and a negative derivative via a strictly decreasing tilted size-biased coordinate mean. The strictly positive quadratic coefficient follows from positive variance. Beta integrals prove all fixed-dimensional algebraic tails; a separate elementary inverse-hyperbolic integral proves the dimension-two logarithmic term. Spherical half-normal convergence and dominated convergence establish the high-dimensional profiles, including their distinct limiting orders. Symbolic and independent quadrature checker passed; finite tests are not treated as proofs.

originality.rationale: The claim assessed for novelty is the combined exact capsule Mahler profile with the sharp plane-only logarithmic second-order tail, all-dimensional algebraic coefficients, quadratic inverse stability, and high-dimensional half-normal crossover. Standard polar integration, Santaló/Blaschke bounds and qualitative shadow-system convexity are credited and explicitly excluded as independent novelty claims. Inspected literature and historical database queries did not reveal an equivalent combination; historical priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: The Euclidean capsule gives a canonical interpolation between a ball (the Mahler-product maximizer) and a long cylinder. Its dimension-dependent second-order profile distinguishes a genuine planar logarithmic anomaly from higher-dimensional algebraic tails; its exact positive quadratic drop gives optimal inverse conditioning, and its Gaussian crossover identifies a noncommuting high-dimensional limit on the sharp d^{-1/2} scale. These combine intrinsic convex-geometric and asymptotic significance beyond a routine single-object volume evaluation.
